title: Accelerator occupancy: 7-day cluster & pool breakout (rolling)
summary: 7-day rolling export showing per-cluster and per-pool accelerator occupancy. Intended for short-term capacity knobs (burst pools, preemptible balancing) and to highlight nightly regional surges. This sheet is a lightweight export from the Console occupancy API for quick review and follow-up tickets.
notes: Export generated from internal occupancy API (console-export-v2) on 2026-05-04 UTC.
Rows are wide CSV strings matching columns above — top_workloads semicolon-separated by estimated GPU-minutes.
This is a working snapshot for quick triage; canonical source is the cluster-level TSDB in Grafana dashboards.
Observed: APAC burst pool shows repeated early-morning peaks (UTC 01:00) aligned with regional traffic from partners.
Observed: us-west batch pool had a one-day spike tied to a scheduled ETL job (ticketed separately).
Open: need to confirm whether embedding-batch jobs are eligible for preemptible rebalancing (see JIRA-INFRA-2147).
derived_insights: APAC burst-short pool has <12% sustained headroom during 00:00-03:00 UTC — recommend temporary burst expansion or offload to reserved during recurring peak.
eu-central interactive pool shows variability tied to business hours; 2 nodes could be consolidated to reclaim 6 GPUs without SLA impact (low latency metrics are still within SLO).
us-east reserved cluster close to 94% on 2026-05-04 due to two large evaluation jobs — schedule staggering recommended for next cycle.
Batch-highmem in us-west has recurring overnight training that drives 80-95% occupancy; investigate prefix caching and KV eviction to reduce avg_seq_len impact.
